sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Marginal tooth of the soldier mandible broad at the base, especially on the left mandible (after the original figure of Emerson & Banks 1957, see Fig. 2A of the original). Short hairs scattered over the head, nasus and postmentum; the dorsal surface of the apical third of the nasus and the posterior part of the head almost bare (after Emerson & Banks 1957: 4). Compared with E. festivellus, the soldier mandibles of this species are stouter overall, the mandibular blade beyond the marginal tooth is longer and more slender, the outer margin of the mandible has a shallow notch, and the nasus is parallel to the mandibles rather than forked.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: Enteric valve composed of three finger-like cushions of unequal length, covered with 80-100 minute spines, with three shorter and broader areas bearing finer spines between them; in this species the spines of the broader areas are grouped (in twos, threes or fours), whereas in E. spissus they are single. This species and E. spissus are the largest in the genus, with a soldier head width of 1.55-1.77 mm (in the original this range is the two species combined).

note: Rewritten from the Identification section of Scheffrahn (Check List 17 (4): 1043); the original is in English. This passage is the diagnostic account of the soldier of this species (mandibles, pilosity, enteric valve); the original gives no measurements for this species: the 1.55-1.77 mm in the text is the soldier head width of E. latidens and E. spissus combined and is noted as such in the body text; the original states that "the measurements of the original description agree with the present material" but gives no figures. OCR: the species name appears in several places as E. /atidens, EF. latidens and FE. /atidens, restored here to E. latidens from context; the caption (D) is the worker enteric valve armature.
